subject.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI

question: Should OpenClaw core own and distribute a separate Rust interactive launcher despite the terminal-first setup direction and existing CLI and companion-app entry points?
rationale: The line-level defects are repairable, but accepting another executable, toolchain, packaging contract, and convenience UX requires explicit long-term product and ownership intent.

options.title: Keep existing entry points
options.body: Decline or close this launcher direction and continue improving the canonical CLI, dashboard, TUI, and companion apps.

options.title: Sponsor the launcher
options.body: Approve core ownership, then require a focused branch with pure delegation, cross-platform packaging, tests, and current-head real-behavior proof.

recommendation.title: Keep existing entry points
recommendation.body: Decline or close this launcher direction and continue improving the canonical CLI, dashboard, TUI, and companion apps.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the canonical surfaces wrapped by the launcher and is best positioned to decide whether another core entry point belongs.
